title: The Fed makes asset purchases depend on market functioning at the effective lower bound
summary: At 8 a.m. Eastern on 23 March, the Federal Open Market Committee directed the New York Fed to buy Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities in quantities determined by how much support those markets needed. The funds-rate target remained at 0–¼%. A series based only on changes in the target would therefore miss the decision. The new instruction concerned how much the Desk could buy in support of orderly trading and monetary transmission to the broader economy. The statement identifies strains in both markets as the problem. It gives no target for a bond yield, mortgage spread or size of the balance sheet.

The commitment makes a distinction between the goal and the operating variable. The Desk received authority to change the quantity purchased. The Committee retained responsibility for judging the appropriate pace at future meetings. If the Desk later bought fewer securities, that observation alone could support several interpretations. Improving liquidity might reduce the amount needed to achieve the same goal. A different policy judgement could also produce a lower purchase pace. To interpret the quantities, a researcher would need contemporaneous evidence about the markets the Committee said it wanted to support.

The unanimous directive explicitly added agency commercial mortgage-backed securities to the purchase programme. That language identifies the agency backing as part of the eligibility condition. It does not extend the commitment to privately issued commercial mortgage securities generally. Distinguishing eligible from ineligible collateral matters for evaluating the decision. A change in commercial-property financing costs may reflect credit concerns about particular buildings or borrowers as well as the marketability of agency-backed securities. The statement singles out the latter securities for purchases. It offers no forecast for property values or losses on commercial mortgages.

Several other instruments had distinct assignments. Term and overnight repurchase operations were to continue supporting dollar funding markets and keeping reserves ample. An outright purchase adds a security to the Fed's portfolio, while a repo makes short-term funding available against collateral. Those operations can address different dealer constraints even when the same type of security is involved. The $30 billion daily per-counterparty limit in the directive applies to overnight reverse repos, offered at 0.00%, subject also to the available Treasury collateral. Applying that limit to outright purchases would misstate both the instrument and the scale of the commitment.

The instructions for managing the existing portfolio also matter when measuring execution. Treasury principal was to roll over at auction, and monthly principal payments on agency debt and agency MBS were to be reinvested in agency MBS. The Desk could use dollar rolls and coupon swaps to facilitate settlement and could make small operational deviations in reinvestment amounts. Gross transactions, the change in holdings and settlement flows therefore answer different questions. Simply summing every transaction would overstate the amount of new support if it included the replacement of maturing assets.

All ten listed members voted for the action by notation. The statement points to additional measures announced separately, so even an event window centred accurately on 8 a.m. could contain more than one policy development. The original document establishes what the Desk was told to do and why. Whether it became easier to trade in size, whether funding costs fell and whether households or firms subsequently obtained better financing are empirical questions. The announcement itself reports no post-release observations.

questions.question: Did the announcement improve the ability to trade securities in size?
questions.detail: Compare executable bid–ask spreads, quoted depth and price impact around 8 a.m. and around subsequent Desk operations. Look separately at recent Treasury issues, older issues and agency mortgage securities. A lower yield with little change in the cost of executing a large sale would say less about smooth functioning than a recovery in depth across trading venues. Check which markets were liquid enough to support each intraday comparison.

questions.question: Can the effects of purchases be distinguished from those of funding support and other announcements?
questions.detail: Match the timing of outright purchases and repo allotments to changes in cash trading and collateral financing conditions. Separate gross buying, net increases in holdings and reinvested principal. Record contemporaneous measures to which the statement points. A common movement across several markets might reflect the package as a whole. Differences linked to the particular security being purchased would provide additional evidence about the purchase channel.

questions.question: Did eligibility for agency commercial mortgage-backed purchases improve financing beyond secondary trading?
questions.detail: Compare agency and otherwise similar private commercial mortgage securities, allowing for guarantees, borrower risk, maturity and pre-event pricing. Then trace issuance, new loan rates and availability across eligible and ineligible borrowers. A narrowing secondary spread would indicate improved market pricing. Better terms on comparable new mortgages, or a measurable increase in credit supply, would provide evidence for the further transmission to households and businesses described by the Committee.
